raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Image responses are encoded as PNG with zlib level 0 by default since #45987. Pillow still runs its adaptive row filter at that level: for every row it tries the PNG filters and keeps the one with the smallest sum (the encoded files use filters 1 and 2). At level 0 the deflate stream is stored, not compressed, so the filter cannot make the file smaller. It only costs time, and the time is on the output rank between the end of the forward and the reply:

| frame | Pillow, `compress_level=0` | unfiltered rows in stored blocks |
|---|---|---|
| 1024x1024 RGBA (Qwen-Image-2.1) | 74.9 ms | 4.3 ms |
| 1280x720 RGB (Cosmos3 T2I) | 60.9 ms | 2.8 ms |

(One core of a Xeon Platinum 8558P, `Pillow` 13.0.0, zlib 1.3.2. OpenCV's level-0 encoder takes 37.0 / 26.5 ms.)

## Modifications

`entrypoints/utils.py`: `_encode_image_frame` writes a uint8 frame with `compress_level == 0` itself: unfiltered rows (filter byte 0) in one `zlib.compress(rows, 0)` IDAT, behind the same IHDR Pillow writes. Any other level, and non-uint8 frames, still go through Pillow.

The PNG is the same image:
- The IHDR is byte-identical. Pillow writes no other chunks on this path (no gAMA, sRGB, pHYs or text), so the only difference is how the IDAT data is filtered and split: one IDAT chunk instead of Pillow's 64 KiB chunks.
- Decoded pixels, mode and `info` are equal for gray, gray + alpha, RGB and RGBA frames.
- The file is slightly smaller (1024x1024 RGBA: 4,195,716 bytes instead of 4,196,804).

Tests:
- `test_output_saving.py`: levels None, 0 and 75 no longer call Pillow's save, level 100 still saves through Pillow at `compress_level=9`, and every saved file decodes to the source frame. On main the uncompressed cases call Pillow and fail.
- `test_image_response_bytes.py`: the returned-bytes test also covers two-channel (gray + alpha) frames.

## Accuracy Tests

The decoded pixels are identical to the frame the pipeline produced, so the served image does not change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Client latency (median of 5 after warmup), main vs this PR, a fresh server per arm, distinct inputs per request; the Qwen arms ran in pairs on two GPUs and swapped GPUs between rounds.

1xH200 (Qwen-Image-2.1, `--performance-mode speed`) and 2xH200 (Cosmos3-Nano T2I, CFG parallel):

| case | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen-Image-2.1 T2I 1024, GPU 0 / GPU 1 | 4.412 / 4.422 s | 4.376 / 4.385 s |
| Qwen-Image-2.1 edit 1024, GPU 0 / GPU 1 | 5.313 / 5.321 s | 5.257 / 5.284 s |
| Qwen-Image-2.1 T2I throughput (4 requests, concurrency 2) | 0.2267 / 0.2264 req/s | 0.2288 / 0.2282 req/s |
| Cosmos3-Nano T2I 720p, round 1 / round 2 | 0.909 / 0.911 s | 0.893 / 0.895 s |

Every PR sample is below every main sample on the same GPU. On the output rank, the time from the end of the forward to the encoded bytes went from 47 ms to 9.7 ms for a 1024x1024 RGBA image (the rest is the uint8 conversion and the device-to-host copy).

B300 (same harness and protocol, B300 commands; the arms ran next to other arms on the same host, so absolute numbers sit ~10-20 ms above an idle host). The tree under test also carried other changes that do nothing for these requests (they act on reference images and the vision tower):

| case | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen-Image-2.1 T2I 1024, GPU 0 / GPU 1 | 2.231 / 2.250 s | 2.193 / 2.204 s |
| Qwen-Image-2.1 T2I throughput, GPU 0 / GPU 1 | 0.4514 / 0.4513 req/s | 0.4610 / 0.4588 req/s |
| Cosmos3-Nano T2I 720p (2 GPUs), round 1 / round 2 | 0.566 / 0.546 s | 0.511 / 0.512 s |

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -14,9 +14,11 @@
 import mmap
 import os
 import queue
+import struct
 import subprocess
 import tempfile
 import threading
+import zlib
 from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
 from contextlib import contextmanager
 from dataclasses import dataclass, field
@@ -1266,6 +1268,38 @@ def save_materialized_output(
     return image_bytes
 
 
+# PNG color type by channel count: gray, gray + alpha, RGB, RGBA
+_PNG_COLOR_TYPES = {1: 0, 2: 4, 3: 2, 4: 6}
+
+
+def _png_chunk(tag: bytes, data) -> bytes:
+    crc = zlib.crc32(data, zlib.crc32(tag))
+    return b"".join((struct.pack(">I", len(data)), tag, data, struct.pack(">I", crc)))
+
+
+def _encode_png_stored(frame: np.ndarray) -> bytes:
+    """an 8-bit PNG of frame with unfiltered rows in stored (uncompressed) deflate blocks
+
+    PIL still filters every row at compress_level 0, which cannot shrink stored
+    blocks; skipping the filter writes the same pixels over ten times faster
+    """
+    height, width = frame.shape[:2]
+    channels = 1 if frame.ndim == 2 else frame.shape[2]
+    rows = np.zeros((height, 1 + width * channels), np.uint8)
+    rows[:, 1:] = frame.reshape(height, width * channels)
+    header = struct.pack(
+        ">IIBBBBB", width, height, 8, _PNG_COLOR_TYPES[channels], 0, 0, 0
+    )
+    return b"".join(
+        (
+            b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n",
+            _png_chunk(b"IHDR", header),
+            _png_chunk(b"IDAT", zlib.compress(rows, 0)),
+            _png_chunk(b"IEND", b""),
+        )
+    )
+
+
 def _encode_image_frame(
     frame: np.ndarray, path: str, output_compression: int | None
 ) -> bytes:
@@ -1278,6 +1312,8 @@ def _encode_image_frame(
             compress_level = max(0, min(9, round(output_compression / 100 * 9)))
         if frame.ndim == 3 and frame.shape[-1] == 1:
             frame = frame[..., 0]
+        if compress_level == 0 and frame.dtype == np.uint8:
+            return _encode_png_stored(frame)
         buffer = io.BytesIO()
         Image.fromarray(frame).save(buffer, format="PNG", compress_level=compress_level)
         return buffer.getvalue()
